name: kelmar
author: weather-and-seasons designer
description:
kelmar v2 (direction: weather and seasons) -- RAIN OVER A GARDEN: THE PLANTS STANDING RIGHT AT
THE EDGE OF A SHOWER. PRIVATE; never shown to players. v1 (challenges/lab/kelmar.v1.json) scored
0 % for all four Opus players in the 7-class / 3-demo format: its clue `..*...Y..*../*2Y1` read as
"a string plus a legend" and three players spent no demo on it. v2 puts the whole scene in the
clue and cuts the rule to one count.

CLUE = THE SCENE ITSELF, 4 or 5 lines:

    ..........................
    ..........................
    ..........................
    _____Y___*__*__Y__Y___*___
    2

2-3 rows of empty sky (dots), then one row of bare earth "_" 26-32 columns wide holding 6-9
plants -- flowers "*" and small trees "Y", at least 3 of each, never closer than 3 columns apart,
never in the outer two columns -- then a line with a single digit N (1-3, drawn 1:2:3,
capped at plants-4 so there are always spare plants). Nothing is labelled: a player who
has never seen a demo sees a garden under an empty sky and a number, and the only sane thing to
send back is that sky with rain drawn in it.

SOLUTION = the rain. The scorer drops blank lines, right-strips, and IGNORES every line that
contains "*", "Y" or a digit (so echoing the clue's ground row and/or its count line is free, and
so is leaving them out). What is left must be at least two sky rows that are IDENTICAL once
mapped -- "#|/'!" are rain, " ._,:" are dry sky, anything else is rejected -- each as long as the
ground row. Every maximal run of rain (a SHOWER) must be 3-6 columns wide, consecutive showers
must be separated by at least 2 dry columns, and there must be at least 2 showers. Sky height
(2+), rain glyph, dry glyph, blank lines and the ground row are all free.

THE RULE (one clause, the sentence a kid says while pointing): exactly N plants stand in the
column immediately left or immediately right of a shower -- dry, right at the edge of the rain,
just missing it. Wet plants never count, however close to the edge they stand; plants two or more
columns clear never count. Flowers and trees are not told apart (see ONE COUNT below). Which
plants, how many showers, how wide, how much of the garden gets wet: all free.

THE 3-6 COLUMN WIDTH CAP IS LOAD-BEARING. With no cap the whole class collapses to "solid rain
with 2-wide holes over N plants", which satisfies the rule by construction (a 2-wide hole at a
plant makes exactly that plant an edge plant): measured 34 % with a cap of 8, 22 % with 7, and
0.0 % with the shipped cap of 6, because 6-wide showers cannot cover a 26-32 column garden.

ONE COUNT, NOT TWO (measured, then chosen). v1 asked for a flowers AND b trees. Blind floor over
random legal pictures: 26.3 % with one count, 13.7 % with two. Two counts is the harder class,
but in a 26-32 column garden only 75 % of demos can show both a flower and a tree at an edge
*and* the three teaching contrasts, and the rule stops being one breath. In the 3-demo format the
demo has to teach in one look, so the second count was dropped and the higher floor kept as the
foothold. The two glyphs stay in the picture as a decoy dimension ("count the flowers at the
edge") that costs a round to kill.

INTENDED PATH. No demo: the clue is a picture, so the natural probe is "rain over the garden".
Freehand rain scores 2.4 % (widths and gaps are usually illegal), but any regular stripe pattern
with width 3-6 and gap >= 2 scores 20-35 %, so a player sweeping formats in round 1 sees the
class is picture-graded and structural, not exact-match. One demo: the grammar arrives whole and
the only question left is what the digit counts. Every shipped demo falsifies "how many got
rained on" / "how many stayed dry" / "how many showers" / "how many are beside the rain" /
"the plant under the last drop" / "two columns clear" (all 8 loud rivals falsified at once in 72 % of
demos; each one individually in 83-100 %), and every demo shows, within 9 columns of each other,
a plant standing on a shower's last WET column (does not count), a plant one column outside a
shower (counts) and a plant two columns clear (does not count). The crack is the sentence a
12-year-old says while pointing: "that one is standing right on the edge of the shower and
staying dry".

WITNESS TABLE (500 fresh clues; every attacker except the demo-less ones knows the grammar
perfectly and rejection-samples legal pictures until its own hypothesis holds, 500 tries/clue):
true rule 100 % | showers with a plant at their edge, counted per SHOWER 79.2 % (the same
insight, one step off; solve() makes the two readings disagree in 83 % of demos) | only the LEFT
edge counts 49.4 % | only the RIGHT edge counts 49.8 % | plants within two dry columns 35.8 % |
best blind sampler over 14 density settings 34.6 % | random legal showers 28.4 % | rain on
exactly N plants 25.8 % | N showers 23.0 % | plants on the last WET column 21.6 % | N showers
each over a plant 19.6 % | demo-less "N showers over N plants" 17.4 % | demo replay (previous
clue's answer) 15.4 % | N plants left dry, rain on all others 14.0 % | exactly two columns clear
14.6 % | beside the rain, wet or dry 9.8 % | one constant picture 4.4 % | demo-less freehand rain
2.4 % | solid rain with 2-wide holes at N plants 0.0 % | rain everywhere 0.0 % | clue returned
unchanged 0.0 % | empty / 'x' / '1'*100 / 4000 chars of junk / text / ground row alone 0.0 %.
No insight-free construction exceeds 35 %; everything above 49 % is the intended relation in a
weaker form (one side of it, or counted per shower instead of per plant).

FAIRNESS FLOOR. Of 20 hand-built "the digit counts THIS relation" laws, on shipped demos:
2.8 survive one demo on average (max 5), 1.4 survive two, 1.1 survive three, and whenever exactly
one law survives three demos it is the true rule (175/175 trials). One demo plus the ~120 probes
a team gets over two rounds is therefore just enough, which is the calibration target.

VALIDATION. quickcheck --seeds 200: OK, no warnings, gen 0.05 ms, score 0.22 ms, solve 46 ms.
solve() scores 1 on 2000/2000 fresh seeds. Scorer vs an independent re-implementation (column
walk, no regex) on 6300 (clue, answer) pairs: 0 disagreements. 2880 junk strings: 0 raises, 0
non-binary, 0 false positives, worst 0.10 ms. Lenient (all 100 %): dots/spaces/underscores for
dry sky, rain as # / | / / / ', a cloud row on top, ground row kept or dropped or altered, count
line kept, blank lines, trailing spaces, CRLF, 2 or 5 sky rows. Strict (all 0 %): one sky row
only, sky rows not identical, empty sky, all rain, a text label. Shifting the sky one column
scores 22 % -- a coincidence rate, not a leniency hole.

Design notes, the brainstorm and the full iteration record: challenges/lab/NOTES_weather.md.
